title: Salesforce standard objects for sales, marketing and service: Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, OpportunityLineItem, OpportunityContactRole, Case, Campaign, CampaignMember, Order, OrderItem, Product2, Pricebook2, PricebookEntry, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Contract, Asset, User, Task, Event
status_note: Read on 17 November 2026 from Salesforce's public Object Reference and Field Reference (developer.salesforce.com, API version 68.0) and checked field by field against them (tests/fixtures/pk1/salesforce_reference.json keeps the names, types and link targets read); written in our own words. One claim rests on a page that could not be read (sf_queue_owner, Salesforce Help) and says so. Table names are the objects' API names in upper case (OPPORTUNITYLINEITEM); columns are the API field names read without case or underscores (AccountId and account_id alike). Custom fields (__c), custom objects and managed packages are not described. Not verified against any org: documented, not verified on rows. Krusgraph is independent and not affiliated with Salesforce or Microsoft.

variants.api_v2: Salesforce standard objects as the Object Reference describes them, landed one table per object with the API field names (a Fabric Salesforce connector or a pipeline). Not verified against any org.

sf_id_field_type.title: Salesforce Object Reference: field types, the ID field type (15-character case-sensitive ids; the 18-character case-safe form every API call returns; OwnerId holds the owning user's id)
sf_id_field_type.note: Read on 17 November 2026. The page says that ids are often shown as 15 case-sensitive characters, that all API calls return an 18-character case-safe id whose last three characters encode the case of the first fifteen, that truncating the last three gives the 15-character form, that an id carries a three-character code for the object type (describeSObjects returns it), and that OwnerId holds the id of the user who owns the record. The old atlas URL (atlas.en-us.api.meta/api/field_types.htm) redirects elsewhere.

sf_queue_owner.title: Salesforce Help: queues own leads, cases and some other records (ownership by a queue instead of a user)
sf_queue_owner.note: Not read: help.salesforce.com renders its articles in the browser, and the writing session (17 November 2026) received the page frame without the article text. Written from public knowledge; the Object Reference pages read that day support it only indirectly (CampaignMember.LeadOrContactOwnerId refers to Queue or User). Unverified.

tables.name: ACCOUNT
tables.en: Salesforce Account (a company, or a person in orgs with person accounts)
tables.sv: Salesforce-konto (ett företag, eller en person där personkonton används)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Account field reference).
tables.note: PARENT_ID names the parent account in a hierarchy (a reference to Account itself). In an org with person accounts an Account row can be a person (IS_PERSON_ACCOUNT), and its name is then personal data; the person fields come from the account's person contact. OWNER_ID is the owning user.

tables.name: CONTACT
tables.en: Contact (a person, usually at an account)
tables.sv: Kontakt (en person, oftast hos ett konto)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Contact field reference).
tables.note: ACCOUNT_ID can be empty (a contact without an account). REPORTS_TO_ID names another contact. Personal data throughout.

tables.name: LEAD
tables.en: Lead (a prospect not yet qualified; converted into an account, a contact and possibly an opportunity)
tables.sv: Lead (ett prospekt som ännu inte kvalificerats; konverteras till konto, kontakt och eventuellt affärsmöjlighet)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Lead field reference).
tables.note: IS_CONVERTED, CONVERTED_DATE and CONVERTED_ACCOUNT_ID, CONVERTED_CONTACT_ID, CONVERTED_OPPORTUNITY_ID record a conversion; a converted lead is read-only afterwards and stays in the table beside the contact it became. COMPANY is the prospect's company as text, not a link. OWNER_ID can be a queue (see the trap).

tables.name: OPPORTUNITY
tables.en: Opportunity (a sale or pending deal)
tables.sv: Affärsmöjlighet (en affär eller pågående affär)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Opportunity field reference).

amounts.currency: CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column

tables.note: With products (OPPORTUNITYLINEITEM) every line item adds its TOTAL_PRICE to AMOUNT, and AMOUNT becomes read-only (the OpportunityLineItem page, 'Effects on Opportunities'); EXPECTED_REVENUE grows by TOTAL_PRICE times PROBABILITY in the same way. Joined with its line items the amount is repeated once per line. STAGE_NAME, IS_CLOSED and IS_WON say where the deal stands; CLOSE_DATE when it closed or is expected to. PRICEBOOK2_ID and CURRENCY_ISO_CODE cannot change once line items exist.

tables.name: OPPORTUNITYLINEITEM
tables.en: Opportunity product (a line of an opportunity: a price book entry, a quantity and a price)
tables.sv: Affärsmöjlighetsprodukt (en rad på en affärsmöjlighet)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (OpportunityLineItem field reference).

amounts.currency: the opportunity's currency (OPPORTUNITY.CURRENCY_ISO_CODE in a multi-currency org; the line's own CURRENCY_ISO_CODE is set from it and cannot be changed)

tables.note: OPPORTUNITY_ID is required and cannot be updated (a line never moves to another opportunity); the page calls it a relationship, not master-detail. The product is chosen through PRICEBOOK_ENTRY_ID, which must be an entry of the opportunity's price book; PRODUCT2_ID is read-only (API 30.0 and later) and the page says to use the price book entry instead. UNIT_PRICE is the sales price, LIST_PRICE the entry's price, TOTAL_PRICE the line's amount.

tables.name: OPPORTUNITYCONTACTROLE
tables.en: Opportunity contact role (a contact's role on an opportunity; one of them can be primary)
tables.sv: Kontaktroll på affärsmöjlighet (en kontakts roll i en affär; en kan vara primär)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (OpportunityContactRole field reference).
tables.note: A link table between OPPORTUNITY and CONTACT with ROLE and IS_PRIMARY: one opportunity has many contacts and one contact many opportunities. Each opportunity has only one primary contact. Counting opportunities through this table counts an opportunity once per contact.

tables.name: CASE
tables.en: Case (a customer's question, problem or request)
tables.sv: Ärende (en kunds fråga, problem eller begäran)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Case field reference).
tables.note: CASE_NUMBER is assigned automatically and cannot be changed. ACCOUNT_ID and CONTACT_ID can name different customers (the page has a section on separating accounts from contacts). PARENT_ID names a parent case. SUPPLIED_* hold what a web or e-mail form sent, before a contact is matched. OWNER_ID can be a queue (see the trap).

tables.name: CAMPAIGN
tables.en: Campaign (a marketing initiative: an event, a mailing, an advertisement)
tables.sv: Kampanj (en marknadsaktivitet)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Campaign field reference).

amounts.currency: CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column
CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column
CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column
CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column

tables.note: AMOUNT_ALL_OPPORTUNITIES and AMOUNT_WON_OPPORTUNITIES are read-only sums Salesforce keeps over the opportunities of the campaign: adding them to OPPORTUNITY.AMOUNT counts the same deals twice, and joined with its opportunities or members they repeat once per row. PARENT_ID names a parent campaign.

tables.name: CAMPAIGNMEMBER
tables.en: Campaign member (a lead or a contact in a campaign, with its response status)
tables.sv: Kampanjmedlem (ett lead eller en kontakt i en kampanj)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (CampaignMember field reference).
tables.note: Each row names a lead (LEAD_ID) or a contact (CONTACT_ID); a row given both keeps only the contact, except when a converted lead is tracked with both. In orgs with accounts as campaign members ACCOUNT_ID can be set instead. STATUS and HAS_RESPONDED say how the member responded.

tables.name: ORDER
tables.en: Order (an agreement to provide products or services; may come from an opportunity or a quote and sit under a contract)
tables.sv: Order (ett avtal att leverera produkter eller tjänster)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Order field reference).

amounts.currency: CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column

tables.note: TOTAL_AMOUNT is the net total of the order's products (ORDERITEM): joined with its lines it is repeated once per line. ORDER_NUMBER is an auto-number, not the id. STATUS is Draft or Activated; only a draft can be deleted. ORIGINAL_ORDER_ID marks a reduction order against an earlier order.

tables.name: ORDERITEM
tables.en: Order product (a line of an order)
tables.sv: Orderprodukt (en orderrad)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (OrderItem field reference).
tables.note: ORDER_ID is required and cannot be updated. As on an opportunity line, the product comes through PRICEBOOK_ENTRY_ID; PRODUCT2_ID cannot be updated after insert. QUOTE_LINE_ITEM_ID names the quote line it came from. The page says TOTAL_PRICE is calculated differently when Commerce Orders are enabled.

tables.name: PRODUCT2
tables.en: Product (the product catalog)
tables.sv: Produkt (produktkatalogen)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Product2 field reference).
tables.note: PRODUCT_CODE is free text and not declared unique. A product has a price only through PRICEBOOKENTRY, one per price book and (in a multi-currency org) currency. QUANTITY_UNIT_OF_MEASURE is the unit of the lines' QUANTITY.

tables.name: PRICEBOOK2
tables.en: Price book (a list of products and their prices)
tables.sv: Prislista (en lista över produkter och deras priser)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Pricebook2 field reference).
tables.note: Every org has one standard price book (IS_STANDARD); the others are custom. Deleting a price book that line items still reference archives it: the lines are unaffected but the price book is no longer available from the API, so it can be missing from a landing while lines point at its entries.

tables.name: PRICEBOOKENTRY
tables.en: Price book entry (a product's price in one price book and currency)
tables.sv: Prislistepost (en produkts pris i en prislista och valuta)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (PricebookEntry field reference).
tables.note: PRICEBOOK2_ID and PRODUCT2_ID are both required. UNIT_PRICE is the list price, not an amount; with USE_STANDARD_PRICE it is the standard price book's.

tables.name: QUOTE
tables.en: Quote (proposed prices of products for a customer, under an opportunity)
tables.sv: Offert (föreslagna priser till en kund, under en affärsmöjlighet)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Quote field reference).

amounts.currency: CURRENCY_ISO_CODE when the org has multi-currency enabled; otherwise the org's corporate currency, and there is no currency column

tables.note: OPPORTUNITY_ID is a master-detail relationship on the page: every quote belongs to one opportunity. TOTAL_PRICE is the total of the quote's line items after discounts and before tax and shipping; GRAND_TOTAL adds shipping and tax; SUBTOTAL is before discounts. The same column name TOTAL_PRICE is a header total here and a line total on QUOTELINEITEM. One quote of an opportunity can be syncing with it (IS_SYNCING; OPPORTUNITY.SYNCED_QUOTE_ID). ACCOUNT_ID is read-only. QUOTE_NUMBER is system-generated.

tables.name: QUOTELINEITEM
tables.en: Quote line item (a line of a quote)
tables.sv: Offertrad (en rad på en offert)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (QuoteLineItem field reference).
tables.note: QUOTE_ID is a master-detail relationship on the page, required and not updatable. TOTAL_PRICE is read-only: SUBTOTAL (QUANTITY times UNIT_PRICE) after the discount. OPPORTUNITY_LINE_ITEM_ID names the opportunity line the quote line mirrors when the quote syncs; it is filled by the API and not editable.

tables.name: CONTRACT
tables.en: Contract (a business agreement with an account)
tables.sv: Kontrakt (ett affärsavtal med ett konto)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Contract field reference).
tables.note: CONTRACT_NUMBER is an auto-number. START_DATE and CONTRACT_TERM (months) give the term, END_DATE follows. ACCOUNT_ID is required. Opportunities and orders can name the contract.

tables.name: ASSET
tables.en: Asset (a product a customer owns or uses, with serial number, dates and price)
tables.sv: Tillgång (en produkt som en kund äger eller använder)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Asset field reference).
tables.note: ACCOUNT_ID and CONTACT_ID say whose asset it is, PRODUCT2_ID what it is. PRICE is what was paid for this asset, not a line of an order: summed with order lines it counts the same sale twice when the asset came from an order. PARENT_ID and ROOT_ASSET_ID build an asset hierarchy.

tables.name: USER
tables.en: User (a person who signs in to the org: owners, sales representatives, case agents)
tables.sv: Användare (en person som loggar in i organisationen)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (User field reference).
tables.note: Every OWNER_ID that names a person points here. MANAGER_ID names another user. USERNAME is the sign-in name. Inactive users (IS_ACTIVE false) stay in the table and keep owning records. Personal data of employees.

tables.name: TASK
tables.en: Task (a to-do or a logged call or e-mail, about a person and a record)
tables.sv: Uppgift (en att-göra-post eller loggat samtal/e-post, om en person och en post)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Task field reference).
tables.note: WHO_ID is polymorphic: a contact or a lead. WHAT_ID is polymorphic: an account, opportunity, case, campaign, contract, order, quote, asset, product or any of some 1 500 other objects the page lists. ACCOUNT_ID is derived and read-only. OWNER_ID is the assigned user. Recurring tasks have a main record and occurrences (RECURRENCE_ACTIVITY_ID).

tables.name: EVENT
tables.en: Event (a calendar meeting about a person and a record)
tables.sv: Händelse (ett kalendermöte om en person och en post)
tables.key_note: Id, the record id: type id, 18 characters through the API (Event field reference).
tables.note: WHO_ID and WHAT_ID are polymorphic as on Task (WhatId is labelled Related To ID on the page). ACCOUNT_ID is derived and read-only. START_DATE_TIME, END_DATE_TIME and DURATION_IN_MINUTES time it.

traps.title: Opportunity.Amount, Order.TotalAmount and Quote.TotalPrice are totals of their lines
traps.text: Every opportunity line item adds its TOTAL_PRICE to OPPORTUNITY.AMOUNT, and AMOUNT is read-only once the opportunity has line items; ORDER.TOTAL_AMOUNT is the net total of the order's products; QUOTE.TOTAL_PRICE the total of the quote's line items after discounts. A header amount summed over a join with its lines counts once per line (the total that doubles). On Quote and QuoteLineItem the same name TOTAL_PRICE is a header total and a line total. UNIT_PRICE and LIST_PRICE are prices, not amounts.

traps.title: The product is reached through the price book entry
traps.text: A line (opportunity, order or quote) names a PricebookEntry, which names the Product2 and the Pricebook2. PRODUCT2_ID on an opportunity line is a read-only copy of the entry's product; read one of them as the link, not both as independent facts. A price book deleted while lines still reference it is archived and no longer available from the API: its entries' PRICEBOOK2_ID can point at nothing in a landing.

traps.title: A currency column exists only in a multi-currency org
traps.text: CURRENCY_ISO_CODE is present only when multi-currency is enabled; a line item's currency is always its opportunity's. Without it every amount is in the org's corporate currency and there is no column to read. A sum over opportunities of several currencies without a conversion adds currencies.

traps.title: Salesforce ids: 15 characters in the user interface, 18 through the API
traps.text: The API returns 18-character, case-safe ids; the user interface and many reports show the 15-character, case-sensitive form, which is the 18-character id without its last three characters. A key pasted or exported in 15 characters finds nothing in a table loaded through the API, and a 15-character id compared without case can match the wrong record. Compare on 18 characters, or on the first 15 compared with case.

traps.title: Task and Event point at different tables from one column
traps.text: WHO_ID is a contact or a lead; WHAT_ID one of some 1 500 object types (an account, an opportunity, a case, ...). A join of WHAT_ID to OPPORTUNITY finds only the activities about opportunities, and the others look like orphans. Split by the id's three-character object prefix (the describeSObjects key prefix of each object) before joining, or use ACCOUNT_ID, which the activity carries already. The pack lists these links and applies none of them.

traps.title: A converted lead stays in the Lead table
traps.text: Converting a lead creates (or matches) an account, a contact and possibly an opportunity, sets IS_CONVERTED and the CONVERTED_* ids, and leaves the lead read-only in the table. Counting leads and contacts together counts a converted person twice; a funnel counts leads, then IS_CONVERTED, then the converted opportunities (CONVERTED_OPPORTUNITY_ID) and their IS_WON.

traps.title: Campaign amounts are sums over its opportunities
traps.text: CAMPAIGN.AMOUNT_ALL_OPPORTUNITIES and AMOUNT_WON_OPPORTUNITIES are read-only sums Salesforce keeps over the campaign's opportunities. Adding them to the opportunities' AMOUNT counts the deals twice, and joined with members or opportunities they repeat once per row. An opportunity counts for one campaign (its CAMPAIGN_ID, the primary campaign source) even when its contacts were members of several.

traps.title: A syncing quote mirrors the opportunity's lines
traps.text: One quote of an opportunity can sync with it (QUOTE.IS_SYNCING, OPPORTUNITY.SYNCED_QUOTE_ID); its lines then mirror the opportunity's line items (QUOTELINEITEM.OPPORTUNITY_LINE_ITEM_ID). Summing quote lines and opportunity lines together counts the same deal twice, and summing all quotes of an opportunity counts every version of the offer.

traps.title: Opportunity contacts are a link table
traps.text: OPPORTUNITYCONTACTROLE links opportunities and contacts many-to-many, with a ROLE and one primary contact per opportunity. An opportunity amount summed through it counts once per contact; filter IS_PRIMARY or count distinct opportunities. OPPORTUNITY.CONTACT_ID is set on create only and does not follow the roles.

traps.title: Deleted records can land too
traps.text: Fabric's Salesforce copy can include deleted records (the copy activity's 'Include deleted objects'); they carry IS_DELETED = true. A landing made with that option counts deleted opportunities, cases and lines unless IS_DELETED is filtered. Opportunity line items deleted directly skip the recycle bin and are not returned at all.

traps.title: An owner is not always a user
traps.text: OWNER_ID holds the owning user's id on most objects; leads and cases can be owned by a queue, whose id is in no USER row. The pack applies OWNER_ID -> USER where the owner is a user and lists it, not applied, for Lead, Case, Task and Event.

traps.title: How Salesforce lands in Fabric: object and field API names, unless someone renamed them
traps.text: Microsoft Learn lists no Salesforce source for Fabric database mirroring (17 November 2026; third-party tools offer open mirroring); the data usually arrives through Data Factory's Salesforce objects connector (Copy job, a pipeline's copy activity reading an object by its API name or a SOQL query, or Dataflow Gen2). A Copy job keeps the source's table and column names and types unless mapped; Dataflow Gen2 names a table after its query and adjusts unsupported characters. So a landing usually reads Account, OpportunityLineItem and AccountId, but a mapping, a prefix (sf_) or a lower-case convention is the integrator's choice; the pack compares names without case and underscores and reads past an sf_ or salesforce_ prefix. ORDER, CASE and USER are reserved words in SQL and need brackets. Custom fields (__c) and custom objects are not described.

traps.title: An account can be a person
traps.text: With person accounts enabled, an ACCOUNT row with IS_PERSON_ACCOUNT true is a person, and its name and the person fields carried from its contact are personal data. A count of accounts as companies then includes people.
